title: Falafel
subtitle: Crisp fried chickpea patties with herbs and spices
excerpt: Chickpeas blended with fresh coriander, parsley, cumin and chilli flakes, then shaped and fried until the outside is deeply golden and crisp while the inside stays tender and herb-flecked. Falafel need no binding egg; the flour and the natural starch of the chickpeas hold them together. The mixture needs to be chilled for 30 minutes before frying for the best results.
sourceNotes: Falafel is believed to have originated in Egypt, where it was made with fava beans; the chickpea version spread across the Levant and became a staple street food throughout the Middle East and beyond.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The unfried mixture can be made and refrigerated for up to 24 hours. Chill for at least 30 minutes before frying for firmer patties.

content.text: Pulse rather than blend the mixture in a food processor. You want a coarse, slightly gritty texture that holds together when pressed, not a smooth paste that turns gluey when fried. The difference between a crumbly falafel and one that holds its shape is chilling the mixture; 30 minutes in the fridge firms it up enough to fry confidently. If the mixture feels too wet to shape, add another tablespoon of flour.

items.prepNote: plus extra if the mixture is too wet

content.text: Combine the drained chickpeas, onion, garlic, fresh coriander, flat-leaf parsley, cumin, ground coriander, chilli flakes and a generous pinch of salt in a food processor. Pulse in short bursts until the mixture is finely chopped and coarse, scraping down the sides as needed. Do not blend smooth.

Tip into a bowl. Add the flour and mix well. The mixture should hold together when pressed into a ball but still feel slightly grainy. If too wet, add another tablespoon of flour. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Shape the mixture into small patties or balls, about 30g each. Use wet hands to prevent sticking.

Pour the sunflower oil into a large, deep saucepan to a depth of at least 5cm. Heat to 180C. To test without a thermometer, drop in a small piece of mixture: it should sizzle immediately and rise to the surface. Fry the falafel in batches of 4 to 5 for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden brown.
Drain on kitchen paper and season immediately with salt. Serve with flatbread, pickles and tahini.

items.symptom: Falafel are falling apart in the oil
items.cause: Mixture was not chilled or needs more flour
items.fix: Remove from the oil, reshape firmly and refrigerate for another 30 minutes. Stir in an extra tablespoon of flour before re-frying.

items.symptom: Falafel are brown outside but doughy inside
items.cause: Oil was too hot, cooking the outside too fast before the inside could set
items.fix: Reduce the oil temperature to around 170C and fry for a longer time. A slightly lower temperature cooks the inside evenly without burning the crust.
